items.item: Each row shows the user's name and email, role, status in words (such as Active, Invited, Deactivated, Locked) and whether two-factor sign-in is enabled
items.evidence: Row markup (renderTable, page.html:469-480) renders name/email (td.py-2.5 pr-3 > div.flex.items-center), roleBadge(u.role), and statusBadge(u.status) with word labels ('Active', 'Pending invite', 'Deactivated'). There is no field, column, icon or data property anywhere for two-factor/MFA status — the user objects in initialUsers (page.html:317-333) have no twoFactor/mfa property and no such indicator is rendered.

items.item: Last sign-in uses one date-time format with the timezone stated, relative times also expose the exact time, and an account that has never signed in shows "Never" rather than a blank or a 1970 date
items.evidence: relativeTime() (page.html:354-367) only outputs strings like '6 mins ago', '3 hours ago', 'Yesterday', '9 days ago', '2 months ago' with no title/tooltip attribute exposing the exact timestamp and no timezone text anywhere on the page. The 'Never' fallback (page.html:463) is dead code for this dataset — pending users instead show 'Invite not accepted', and no active user has a null lastSignIn, so the never-signed-in/'Never' case is never actually exercised.

items.item: Users can be found by searching name or email and filtered by role, status and inactivity (such as no sign-in for 90+ days), with the number of matching users shown
items.evidence: #search-input filters name/email (getFiltered, page.html:408-416), #role-filter and #status-filter exist, and #row-count shows 'Showing X of Y accounts' (page.html:444). However there is no inactivity/no-sign-in-90+-days filter control anywhere in the controls bar (only role-filter and status-filter selects exist, page.html:143-156).

items.item: The invite form requires an email and a role, labels both fields, and shows an inline error for a malformed address or one that already has an account
items.evidence: #invite-email is required with a <label for="invite-email"> and #invite-role has a <label for="invite-role"> (page.html:225-236). The submit handler (page.html:629-638) only checks a regex for malformed format and shows #invite-email-error; there is no check against existing users' emails, so inviting an address that already has an account produces no inline error (it would silently create a duplicate user via users.unshift).

items.item: Deactivation asks for confirmation that names the user and states the effect (active sessions ended, sign-in blocked, data kept), and a deactivated user is offered Reactivate instead
items.evidence: openDeactivateDialog (page.html:657-682) sets the title to 'Deactivate {name}?' and body to "They'll be signed out immediately and lose access until reactivated. This can be undone." — this names the user and covers sessions-ended/sign-in-blocked, but never states that their data is kept. Reactivate is correctly offered for already-deactivated users (title becomes 'Reactivate {name}?', confirmLabel 'Reactivate').

items.item: The signed-in administrator's own row is marked (such as "You") and cannot be deactivated or lose the admin role, and the last remaining administrator cannot be deactivated, with the disabled action explaining why
items.evidence: The signed-in admin 'Alex Donovan' only appears in the sidebar footer (page.html:79-84) and has no row in the users table (initialUsers, page.html:317-333, contains no u matching 'Alex Donovan'), so no row is marked 'You'. openDeactivateDialog/deactivate-confirm (page.html:657-702) contain no logic checking current-admin identity, role counts, or disabling the action for the last remaining admin.

items.item: Password reset sends a reset link to the user's email address, which the confirmation names, and the administrator never sees, sets or types the new password
items.evidence: openResetDialog titles the dialog 'Send password reset to {name}?' (page.html:713-721) and on confirm shows toast 'Reset link sent to {email}.' (page.html:723-734). No password input field exists anywhere in the reset flow.

items.item: Row actions are buttons or a keyboard-operable menu whose accessible names include the user (such as "Actions for Mai Nguyen"), and the outcome of an action is announced in an aria-live or role="status" region
items.evidence: The trigger button has aria-label="Actions for ${u.name}" (page.html:482), satisfying the accessible-name requirement. But the toast used for outcomes, `<div id="toast" class="hidden fixed bottom-5 right-5 ...">` (page.html:305-308), has no aria-live or role="status" attribute, so action outcomes (invite sent, deactivated, reset link sent) are not announced to assistive tech.

items.item: A search with no matching users shows a message with a way to clear it, and loading and failed-load states with a retry exist
items.evidence: #empty-state (page.html:188-195) shows 'No matching accounts' with only an 'Invite someone →' link — there is no 'Clear search'/'Clear filters' control to reset the query. No loading-state markup is used (the .skeleton CSS class at page.html:41 is defined but never applied to any element) and there is no failed-load/error state or retry button anywhere in the page or script.

tells: glass — header uses `bg-white/90 backdrop-blur` (page.html:91), flagged by the audit's no-backdrop-blur rule (blur(8px) found, expected none)
notes: Data/markup only exposes name, email, role, status and relative last-sign-in; there is no two-factor/MFA field, no inactivity filter, no current-admin/last-admin protection, and the outcome toast lacks aria-live/role=status. Automated audit (score 72/100) separately flags text-contrast failures on several avatar/badge/muted-text elements, missing mailto: links for emails, and two-line table rows.
